title: Observation of long-lived spin order in nanoconfined water
authors: Rohma Khan, Kang Xu, Nathaniel Jeffries, Ankit Bhardwaj, Boya Radha, Daniela Pagliero, Carlos A. Meriles
abstract: Liquids confined to nanometer-scale geometries exhibit behavior that departs markedly from their bulk counterparts, yet studying their dynamics under controlled conditions remains experimentally challenging. Here, we use nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy to probe water confined in 5.6 nm channels as a function of temperature. The system remains liquid throughout the investigated temperature range and exhibits strongly suppressed diffusivity, enabling direct detection of its 1H NMR spectrum. Occasionally, the proton resonance transforms into a doublet with a splitting of several tens of kilohertz, which we tentatively attribute to hyperfine interactions mediated by long-lived paramagnetic charge complexes, in turn seeded by solvated electrons optically injected during laser illumination. The intermittent appearance of this feature suggests a metastable state comprising a correlated population of charge-hydration complexes extending throughout the confined liquid.
summary: This paper uses NV-NMR spectroscopy on nanoconfined water to observe a transient, resolved proton doublet, indicating unusual spin order. The authors develop a theoretical model based on minimizing free energy to explain this state as arising from extended, correlated charge-hydration complexes. It provides insights into the complex interplay between confinement, electrostatics, and liquid structure at the nanoscale.
main_problem: The study investigates the unusual spin order observed in water confined to nanometer channels, aiming to understand the interplay between local electric fields, charge accumulation, and molecular mobility.
main_result: The intermittent appearance of a resolved proton doublet suggests a metastable state involving a spatially extended, correlated population of charge-hydration complexes within the liquid.
method: The research combines NV-NMR spectroscopy measurements with theoretical modeling that minimizes a Helmholtz free energy functional to predict equilibrium charge profiles.
model_or_system: The system is water confined in $\sim 5.6$ nm channels, probed using NV-NMR. The model treats the liquid as a slab where mobile paramagnetic charges interact electrostatically and are constrained by hydration penalties.
key_observables: Proton NMR linewidth (diffusivity), appearance/evolution of a resolved doublet splitting ($\sim 30 	ext{ kHz}$), and the order parameter tracking spectral changes over hours.
important_parameters: Temperature dependence, confinement width ($5.6 	ext{ nm}$), hyperfine coupling strength, and timescales ranging from microseconds to hours.
main_assumptions: The model assumes translational invariance laterally and that the system can be described by minimizing a Helmholtz free energy functional incorporating electrostatic and hydration terms.
figures_summary: Figures show temperature-controlled setups, ODMR spectra, ${}^1	ext{H}$ NMR spectra demonstrating linewidth suppression and doublet formation, and time evolution plots tracking the order parameter $\Phi$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from initial experimental observations of suppressed dynamics to identifying the transient doublet feature. It then develops a theoretical framework using free energy minimization to model the charge distribution responsible for this spin ordering.
why_interesting: The work bridges quantum sensing (NV-NMR) with complex many-body physics in confined liquids, providing insights into non-equilibrium structural phases stabilized by electrostatics and hydrogen bonding.
